declaration.preface:
Shenzhen Xingbiao Electronic Technology Co Ltd places ethical conduct at the heart of our corporate identity. This policy outlines our commitment to upholding honesty, fairness, and legal compliance in every aspect of our operations. It serves as a practical framework for making responsible choices and conducting business with integrity.

We understand that consistent ethical behaviour builds lasting credibility with our employees, customers, suppliers, and broader stakeholders. By integrating ethical values into our daily decision-making and business processes, we cultivate a workplace culture based on professionalism, accountability, and mutual respect. Every individual at Shenzhen Xingbiao Electronic Technology Co Ltd is expected to embody these principles at all times.
declaration.declaration:
Shenzhen Xingbiao Electronic Technology Co Ltd is firmly committed to conducting its business with honesty, integrity, and a strong sense of responsibility. We believe that ethical behaviour is not just a requirement but a core element of who we are as an organization. Every team member, including employees, contractors, and business partners, is expected to uphold these values in all professional activities.

Our commitment to ethical excellence is reflected in our efforts to educate our workforce, encourage responsible practices, and ensure that ethical considerations are integrated into both daily operations and long-term planning. We strive to maintain a work culture where doing the right thing is second nature.
declaration.scope: This policy applies to all employees, workers, subcontractors, and other stakeholders directly affiliated with us. The applicable sites include:

focusAreas: Fair Play: Managing Conflicts of Interest

Secure and Responsible Information Manag: Safeguard the confidentiality of client and partner information through robust data protection controls.
Adopt secure and compliant methods for data handling, including collection, usage, and storage, in line with relevant privacy legislation.
Continuously enhance cybersecurity systems to defend against unauthorized access and potential data leaks.
Educate staff regularly on privacy obligations and secure handling of information to prevent security incidents.
Anti-Bribery and Corruption: Forbid offering or accepting bribes, kickbacks, or improper gifts that could compromise objective business decisions.
Maintain secure and anonymous reporting channels for employees to raise concerns about unethical conduct without fear of reprisal.
Enforce a strict no-tolerance approach to bribery, corruption, money laundering, and conflicts of interest across all company functions.
Provide ongoing training to ensure all personnel understand anti-corruption obligations and adhere to regulatory and ethical expectations.
Ethical Leadership and Accountability: Promote integrity-driven leadership that sets a strong example of ethical behaviour throughout the organization.
Equip employees with resources and guidance to navigate ethical challenges confidently and responsibly.
Establish clear expectations and accountability measures to ensure all team members act in accordance with company values.
Fair Play: Managing Conflicts of Interes: The Company is committed to fair play, transparency, and integrity in all business decisions.
All employees are required to avoid situations where personal interests may conflict, or appear to conflict, with company interests.
The Company promotes open communication and ethical decision-making to prevent conflicts of interest.
Regular internal communication is used to enhance awareness and understanding of conflict of interest risks and expectations.
Leadership is expected to set an example by adhering to higher standards of disclosure and ethical conduct.
Clean Transactions: Combating Money Laun: The Company is committed to preventing any direct or indirect involvement in money laundering or related financial crimes.
All business transactions are conducted with transparency, integrity, and compliance with applicable anti-money laundering (AML) laws and regulations.
Employees are expected to understand money laundering risks relevant to their roles and to act responsibly when handling financial transactions.
Cooperation with regulatory authorities and law enforcement agencies is supported to strengthen AML awareness and compliance.
AML policies and controls are periodically reviewed and strengthened to reflect regulatory and business changes.
Transparency Matters: Preventing Fraud: The Company is committed to full transparency, integrity, and ethical conduct in all business activities.
Fraud in any form is strictly prohibited, and preventive controls are embedded in business operations.
Confidential and secure fraud reporting mechanisms are maintained, with zero tolerance for retaliation.
Ethical behaviour and integrity are regularly reinforced through leadership communication and training.
Anti-Corruption: No employee shall offer, give, request, or accept bribes, kickbacks, facilitation payments, or inappropriate gifts that could influence business decisions.

Refusing cash, gift cards, or expensive entertainment offered by PCB material suppliers, SMT equipment vendors, or inspection service providers in exchange for preferred supplier selection or order allocation.
Conflict of Interest: Employees must disclose any personal, financial, or family interests that could influence or appear to influence company decisions.
Not awarding PCB fabrication, component sourcing, or surface-treatment contracts to a supplier owned by a relative without formal disclosure and management approval.
Confidentiality & Data Protection: Confidential customer, design, and business information must be protected and used only for authorized purposes.
Not sharing customer PCB layouts, Gerber files, BOMs, test programs, pricing, or production volumes with unauthorized parties or competitors.
Fair Competition: The company competes fairly and does not engage in collusion, price-fixing, bid-rigging, or unfair market practices.
Avoiding agreements with other PCB or PCBA manufacturers to fix prices, divide customers, or coordinate bids for electronics clients.
Responsible Sourcing: Suppliers must be selected based on quality, cost, compliance, and ethical practices, not personal benefits.
Selecting laminate, copper foil, solder paste, and electronic component suppliers through approved evaluation processes rather than personal relationships.
Intellectual Property Protection: Customer and company intellectual property must be respected and protected at all times.
Not copying customer PCB designs or using them for other clients without written authorization.
Compliance with Laws & Regulations: All operations must comply with applicable laws, including environmental, labor, product safety, and trade regulations.
Ensuring RoHS, REACH, and applicable export control requirements are met for PCBA, LED products, and consumer electronics.
Product Integrity & Quality Ethics: Products must meet agreed specifications and quality standards without falsification or misrepresentation.
Not bypassing electrical testing, AOI, or functional testing to meet shipment deadlines.
Health, Safety & Environment (HSE) Integ: Employees must follow HSE rules and report unsafe or non-compliant practices.
Reporting improper chemical handling, solder fume control issues, or waste disposal violations in PCB manufacturing processes.
Disciplinary Measures for Policy Violati: The Company shall take prompt, fair, and appropriate action against any violations of this Governance and Ethics Policy. All disciplinary actions will be carried out in accordance with applicable China labour laws, including the Employment Act 1955 (and its amendments), as well as the Company’s internal policies and procedures.
Verbal Warning – For minor, first-time breaches of policy.
Written Warning – For repeated or moderate violations, recorded in the employee’s personnel file.
Suspension Without Pay – For serious misconduct while an investigation is conducted.
Demotion or Removal from Duties – Where trust or competency is compromised.
Termination of Employment – For severe breaches, such as theft, bribery, falsification of records, harassment, or wilful policy violations.
Legal Action – Where a violation involves criminal activity (e.g., fraud, corruption, theft of trade secrets), the matter will be reported to law enforcement.

Employees are encouraged to report violations in good faith through the company’s confidential reporting channels. Any retaliation against whistle-blowers is strictly prohibited and will itself be treated as a serious policy breach.
